action: Upgrade Ruby to 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14. Do not compile or match regular expressions from untrusted input, and plan to move off Ruby 3.2 and earlier, which get no fix.
exec: Ruby is widely used for web back ends; apps that handle untrusted text or patterns could be open to memory-corruption flaws, and Ruby 3.2 and older get no fix.
plain: The Ruby language team released fixes for seven memory-safety bugs. Some could let an attacker run code in apps that handle untrusted text or patterns.

key_findings: Seven flaws in Regexp and String case conversion, tracked as GHSA IDs because CVE IDs were still requested.
Several could allow remote code execution in some scenarios, notably where attacker-controlled patterns are compiled.
Maintainers say they are aware of proof-of-concept code that shows remote code execution for some; GBHackers says the disclosure reported no active exploitation.
Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life and will not be fixed.

sources.name: GBHackers (Ruby2Shell write-up of the Veria Labs disclosure)

summary: The Ruby project announced fixes for seven memory-safety flaws in Regexp and String case conversion, affecting Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 to 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 to 4.0.9. Several could allow remote code execution in some scenarios, and maintainers know of proofs of concept. SecurityWeek says Ruby2Shell (CVE-2026-132825, CVSS 7.4) was disclosed by Veria Labs; Ruby says CVEs are not yet assigned. Fixed in 4.0.10, 3.4.13, 3.3.14.
title: Ruby fixes seven memory-safety flaws in Regexp and String case conversion

validation.note: Ruby advisory read in full; SecurityWeek (20 Nov) and GBHackers independently report Ruby2Shell and the same fixed versions.

review.note: Compared with Ruby advisory and oss-security copy (18 Nov), SecurityWeek (20 Nov): seven flaws, affected and fixed versions, PoC wording, no CVEs at publication, Ruby2Shell CVE-2026-132825 CVSS 7.4 attributed to SecurityWeek, 3.2 EOL.
